title: sys_regmap
description: The GLOBAL/system-control register map -- the asset-processing table's row-8 artifact ('Global register file -> sys_regmap.json: clock/reset/mux/pinmux control bits -> mode-determining bits'). This is deliberately a SEPARATE schema from register_map.schema.json rather than a flag added to it, because the two answer different questions and have different consumers: register_map.schema.json describes the DUT's own functional registers (consumed by address decode and get_register), while this file describes the chip-level bits that decide whether the DUT is clocked, out of reset, and muxed onto the pins at all. register_map.schema.json's flat `blocks` array has no field that could express 'this block is the clock-enable/pinmux/PHY-select block', which is exactly why row 8 was BLOCKED. Like register_map.schema.json this is an INPUT CONTRACT -- transcribed from a real chip-level programming guide or exported from a real system RAL model, never invented by this harness. What IS generated is the classification and the Gate-2 precondition derived from it (dv_harness/sys_regmap.py).

blocks.description: One entry per system-control register block (CRU/PMU/SYSCFG/PINMUX/...).

kind.description: The system function this block governs. This is the field register_map.schema.json has no equivalent of -- it is what makes a block's bits identifiable as mode-determining rather than functional.

control_kind.description: What this bit actually decides. Every entry EXCEPT not_mode_determining is a mode-determining bit: a bit whose value changes whether an interface is clocked / out of reset / connected to the pins at all, and therefore a precondition for interpreting any Gate-2 zero-time connectivity result. not_mode_determining exists so a real programming guide's non-control bits can be transcribed faithfully in the same file instead of being silently dropped.

required_value.description: The value this field must hold for the interface named in `governs_interfaces` to be operational, when the programming guide states one. null when genuinely not documented -- never a guessed placeholder.

governs_interfaces.description: Names of the DUT interfaces this bit gates. An empty list means the programming guide did not scope it to a specific interface; a Gate-2 precondition check treats an unscoped mode-determining bit as applying to every interface, since assuming it is irrelevant would be the unsafe direction.

access_kind.description: Same RAL/IP-XACT-style access encoding as register_map.schema.json, deliberately identical so the two files can be read by one consumer without a translation layer.
